# evoke

> Software, by reflex. `evoke` turns a sentence into a call of a small program. That program is a reflex: a recipe anyone can write, share and improve. A classifier chooses it, and a confidence gate decides whether it runs. A sentence can choose a program. It can never invent a value.

One tool, three ways in: a CLI you talk to, a package manager that installs reflexes from git, and a TypeScript SDK that puts the same decisions inside an application. The classifier is Jev, TypeSafe AI's System One model, which answers closed questions with calibrated probabilities, reached through two built-in adapters: `jev`, TypeSafe AI's own API, and `openjev`, OpenJEV's public door to the same model. The questions, and the gate, are `evoke`'s, and the core names no engine. The current release is {version}. Every page of the manual below is linked as the markdown it was made from, and the whole manual is one file at https://evoke.build/llms-full.txt.

```text
$ evoke "kill the lights in the den"
  lights room="den" state="off"  0.85
den lights off
```

What holds, in any description of `evoke`:

- Every argument has one source: an option the author listed, a word from the user's own vocabulary, or a piece of the sentence read by code and checked against its range. Injected text can choose a call. It can never mint a value.
- The confidence is the weakest answer, and every answer is a calibrated probability. A `read` reflex runs at 0.6, a `write` at 0.8, and a `destructive` reflex always asks. There is no `--yes`. The bars are lines in a file the user owns.
- When it is not sure, it asks. When nothing fits, it abstains and shows the ranking. The user teaches it with one line in an overlay, which no update touches.
- Git is the registry. A reflex is pinned by tag, commit and content hash. No code runs at install time. A fetched reflex runs as the user, and there is no sandbox yet.
- One request per decision leaves the machine, to the classifier, with the user's own key: the sentence, and the questions built from the installed manifests. Nothing reaches evoke.build, which sets no cookie and runs no analytics.
- The reflex format is frozen at version 1, and every promise in the manual is a transcript that runs in CI.
- Apache-2.0; the collection is MIT. The name and the logo are trademarks: except for displaying the licence details and identifying us as the origin of the software, there is no right under the licence to use them.

Install with `curl -fsSL https://evoke.build/install.sh | sh` on macOS or Linux, and `npm install @evoke-build/evoke` for the SDK. Reflexes written in JavaScript need Node 24 or newer. Deciding needs a key: from https://typesafe.ai in `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for the `jev` adapter, or from https://openjev.sh in `OPENJEV_API_KEY` for `openjev`.

## The site

- [The idea](https://evoke.build/idea.html): why reflexes, in ten minutes: the problem trust poses, the move, the number, real sessions where nothing ran on a guess, the recipe, your words, a weave, and where it goes.
- [Use cases](https://evoke.build/use-cases.html): seven real sessions, an ops channel, an inbox, a payments desk, a plant floor, a runbook, a lesson and a weave, each as files anyone can install and as code an app keeps.
- [The reflex format](https://evoke.build/format.html): the format as a specification, version 1, frozen, with its schemas served at https://evoke.build/schemas/reflex.json and beside it.
- [Frequently asked questions](https://evoke.build/faq.html): what a reflex is, what the number means, what it needs, where reflexes come from, what leaves your machine, and who makes it.
- [Privacy policy](https://evoke.build/privacy.html): no cookie, no analytics, no account, nothing held by us; what one request carries and what never travels; what stays on the machine, and how to forget it.

{manual}

## Optional

- [The whole manual in one file](https://evoke.build/llms-full.txt): every page above in reading order, each under its address, every link absolute.
- [Repository](https://github.com/evoke-build/evoke): the source, the executable spec, the changelog and the releases.
- [The collection](https://github.com/evoke-build/reflexes): the first-party reflexes, what a Mac does at a word.
- [The SDK on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@evoke-build/evoke): `@evoke-build/evoke`, Node 24.5 or newer, ES modules, no dependencies.
- [Jev](https://typesafe.ai): TypeSafe AI's classifier, the first adapter.
- [OpenJEV](https://openjev.sh): an independent project's public door to Jev, the `openjev` adapter.
